pairs.question: Cur igitur ab eo, quod est "edo" et "ungo", in quibus verbis prima littera breviter dicitur, "esito" et "unctito", quae sunt eorum frequentativa, prima littera longa promimus et contra "dictito" ab eo verbo, quod est "dico", correpte dicimus? num ergo potius "actito" et "actitavi" producenda sunt?
pairs.answer: Sic igitur "actito" producte in prima syllaba pronuntiandum, quoniam ex eo fit, quod est "ago" et "actus".
pairs.derivation: Author poses the rhetorical question and answers it himself. Question span runs from the interrogative "Cur igitur... dicimus?" through the operative "num ergo potius... producenda sunt?". The intervening reasoning (the list of frequentatives "quoniam frequentativa ferme omnia... factito") is digression/argumentation, not the answer; the answer window is the concluding answering sentence beginning "Sic igitur", which directly resolves the question. Section markers (I., II., III.) stripped.

pairs.question: Quis enim e medio facile dixerit infestum esse, cui alter infestus est?
pairs.answer: Sed et veteres plerique ita dixerunt, et M. Tullius in oratione, quam Pro Cn. Plancio scripsit, vocabulo hoc sic usus est.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the rhetorical question (no ordinary speaker would readily call a man infestus toward whom another is infestus) and answers it himself: the ancients did say it, with Cicero cited. Answer ends at the first full stop before the verbatim Cicero quotation begins ("Dolebam inquit iudices..."), which is illustration rather than the answer itself. Section markers (IV., V.) stripped.
